# Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait — facts

## Definitions

- [statement] The INVEST publication is a protocol for a planned open-label randomized comparison of DBS and continuous intrajejunal levodopa, with ancillary preference cohorts and quality-of-life and economic outcomes. Its planned sample and methods must not be cited as completed efficacy or cost-effectiveness results. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6995127/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS

## Structure and components

- [statement] The 2026 referral consensus states that the degree of symptom responsiveness to levodopa should be assessed and considered but should not be the only criterion for candidacy; a 2020 selection review recommends the levodopa challenge test as a key presurgical tool, states that the rule of UPDRS part-III improvement greater than 30% should not be strictly applied, and notes that patients with disabling dopa-resistant tremor could represent an exception. (medium confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01241-3 · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7761824/

## How it works

- [statement] When substantial dopaminergic medication reduction is the main surgical goal, evidence and the CNS guideline favor STN over GPi; medication reduction remains an individualized objective. (medium confidence) — https://www.cns.org/guidelines/congress-of-neurological-surgeons-systematic-revie/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01015-x
- [statement] When medication reduction is not anticipated and suppressing on-medication dyskinesia is the goal, the CNS guideline favors GPi; GPi can have a direct antidyskinetic effect while medication is maintained. (medium confidence) — https://www.cns.org/guidelines/congress-of-neurological-surgeons-systematic-revie/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK536714/
- [statement] Complete withdrawal of dopaminergic medication after STN DBS is discouraged in the programming review because a hypodopaminergic state can cause apathy and depression, sometimes delayed for weeks; medication adjustment and stimulation adjustment should be coordinated. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558426/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming
- [statement] A 2020 selection review describes levodopa-resistant axial symptoms as a relative contraindication for surgery, while the 2026 referral consensus states that axial symptoms and freezing of gait should not be the sole indication for DBS but, when levodopa-responsive and associated with disabling motor fluctuations, may benefit from appropriately targeted and individualized DBS approaches and should not be viewed as absolute contraindications to surgery. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7761824/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01241-3
- [statement] A programming review states that rigidity is typically used to judge the effect of STN-DBS because it does not fluctuate, responds to stimulation adjustments within seconds and does not depend on patient fatigue or cooperation, that no single clinical sign should be used alone to judge the therapeutic effect, and that the contact with the lowest threshold for beneficial effects and the widest therapeutic window is then selected for chronic stimulation. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558426/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming
- [statement] Device-aided therapy is considered when oral or transdermal treatment inadequately controls disabling motor fluctuations or dyskinesia; options include apomorphine infusion, intestinal levodopa infusion, subcutaneous levodopa infusion and DBS. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11875732/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7592668/
- [statement] Important burdens differ by modality: apomorphine can cause skin nodules, nausea and hypotension; intestinal levodopa can cause tube obstruction or displacement and abdominal complications; subcutaneous foslevodopa can cause infusion-site reactions or infections; DBS carries surgical and hardware risks. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11875732/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7592668/
- [statement] Device-aided therapy is considered when optimized oral treatment no longer adequately controls Parkinson motor complications; the established options include DBS, continuous subcutaneous apomorphine and intestinal levodopa infusion, with subcutaneous foslevodopa/foscarbidopa adding another delivery option. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3825542/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11502575/
- [statement] The 2024 pallidotomy meta-analysis pooled post-treatment changes against baseline in a single-arm analysis because it could not compare against a sham/control group. Its pooled improvements therefore should not be interpreted as sham-adjusted treatment effects. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11422448/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy
- [statement] Thalamotomy can cause persistent neurological deficits. The randomized trial reported persistent paresthesia and ataxia, and the prescriber information describes serious hemiparesis linked to edema and lesion extension toward the internal capsule. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5822192/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S006D.pdf

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The FDA February 28, 2025 roundup reported marketing approval of a software update providing adaptive DBS that adjusts stimulation from detected brain signals. The roundup described use in levodopa-responsive Parkinson disease with symptoms inadequately controlled by medication for at least four years; this historical announcement should not substitute for current device-specific labeling. - [statement] FDA's PMA database record for Medtronic supplement P960009/S478 (Activa, Percept and SenSight Deep Brain Stimulation Therapy System) lists a decision date of 02/20/2025 and an approval order statement for a new optional programming feature called adaptive deep brain stimulation (aDBS), within the indication of adjunctive therapy for levodopa-responsive Parkinson's disease of at least 4 years' duration that is not adequately controlled with medication. - [statement] The registry record for NCT07398157, a University of California, San Francisco interventional trial titled "Simplified, Scalable, 24-hour Adaptive DBS in Parkinson's Disease", lists overall status RECRUITING (status verified 2026-09), an actual start date of 2026-04-09, an estimated enrollment of 24 and an estimated primary completion date of 2029-11-30; its summary says researchers will compare study-derived adaptive DBS settings with clinically programmed continuous DBS settings. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT07398157 · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads
- [statement] The 2026 expert consensus on referral for DBS states that patients with Parkinson's disease supported by the IPMDS clinical diagnostic criteria should be considered for DBS surgery evaluation in situations that include troublesome motor fluctuations and/or dyskinesia that interfere with functioning or quality of life despite optimal medical management, or disabling tremor that is refractory to an adequate levodopa trial. (medium confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01241-3 · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5632902/
- [statement] The 2026 referral consensus states that pre-DBS assessments should include neurological, neurosurgical and neuropsychological evaluations and discussion of the patient's and family's goals and expectations, and that evaluation by an interdisciplinary team is the optimal approach for selecting DBS candidates; a review of patient and target selection adds that preoperative neuropsychiatric and neuropsychological assessment is necessary for risk stratification and that psychiatric clinical stability and social support should be determined before surgery. (medium confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01241-3 · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK536714/, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01015-x
- [statement] For candidates with substantial concern about cognitive decline or depression, the CNS guideline advises considering GPi over STN while weighing the other goals of surgery; this is risk-based selection, not a guarantee of cognitive or mood safety. (medium confidence) — https://www.cns.org/guidelines/congress-of-neurological-surgeons-systematic-revie/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK536714/
- [statement] The 2026 referral consensus states that gait impairment, freezing of gait and imbalance should not be the primary indications for surgery, that the risk of potential worsening of balance should be discussed with patients pre-operatively, and that DBS is unlikely to improve speech and speech impairment is a potential side effect of stimulation. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01241-3 · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming
- [statement] A 2025 review of DBS selection and programming states that programming begins once lead placement is confirmed and hardware integrity is ensured through an impedance check, that programming usually begins 3 to 4 weeks after lead implantation because microlesion effects can cause transient motor improvement, and that brief programming sessions can capture acute side effects but may fail to identify the full range of side effects that emerge with chronic stimulation. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01015-x · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming
- [statement] In the 36-month randomized-trial follow-up, quality-of-life gains diminished and cognitive measures declined despite maintained motor improvement; sustained motor benefit should not be equated with arresting disease progression. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3385495/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming
- [statement] The 2022 EAN/MDS-ES guideline on invasive therapies states that GPi-DBS can also be offered for advanced Parkinson's disease with fluctuations, that for early Parkinson's disease with early fluctuations STN-DBS is likely to improve motor symptoms and quality of life and can be offered, and that DBS should not be offered to people with early Parkinson's disease without fluctuations. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35791766/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming
- [statement] Apomorphine pump continuation is a separate outcome from motor benefit: a retrospective 110-patient study reported 35% discontinuation over two years and stable quality of life among continuers despite sustained motor-fluctuation reduction; another 208-patient cohort found that many discontinuations were switches to DBS, so discontinuation is not synonymous with drug failure. (medium confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-021-00194-7 · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13347506/
- [statement] A 2013 expert review states that very few comparative studies have evaluated the three device-aided therapies for specific motor problems and identifies the type of motor problems, age, and cognitive and psychiatric status as variables relevant to choosing among DBS, apomorphine infusion and duodenal/jejunal levodopa infusion. A 2024 review of advanced therapies states that there is no age limit for LCIG/LECIG and CSAI while an age limit for DBS is often discussed, that dementia is a clear contraindication for CSAI and DBS, that severe orthostatic hypotension and severe psychosis are contraindications for CSAI, and that frequent falls with injuries might be a contraindication for DBS. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3825542/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11502575/
- [statement] Apparent differences between device therapies in observational comparisons require caution: baseline differences can confound outcomes, and retrospective matching cannot remove all selection effects. The 2025 cohort also lacked systematic safety-data collection, preventing a full benefit-risk comparison. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10310730/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS · also: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01093-x

- [statement] The 2022 EAN/MDS-ES guideline on invasive therapies states that STN-DBS is the best-studied intervention for advanced Parkinson's disease with fluctuations not satisfactorily controlled with oral medications and that treatment should be offered to eligible patients, that GPi-DBS can also be offered, that DBS should not be offered to people with early Parkinson's disease without fluctuations, and that LCIG and an apomorphine pump can be considered for advanced Parkinson's disease with fluctuations not sufficiently managed with oral treatments. - [statement] Focused ultrasound thalamotomy is an ablative treatment directed at medication-refractory tremor in tremor-dominant Parkinson disease; pallidotomy targets GPi for motor complications, including dyskinesia. ## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Oehrn and colleagues reported improved motor symptoms and quality of life versus clinically optimized continuous DBS in a blinded randomized crossover feasibility trial involving four male patients. Their personalized feedback markers were stimulation-entrained gamma oscillations in the subthalamic nucleus or motor cortex; the authors called for larger trials. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11826929/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads
- [statement] ADAPT-PD enrolled 68 participants previously stable on continuous DBS and medication. Its comparison of adaptive versus continuous DBS was open-label; randomization and blinding compared the two adaptive modes in participants tolerating both. The study therefore does not establish blinded randomized superiority of adaptive over continuous DBS. (low confidence) — https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaneurology/fullarticle/2839117 · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads
- [statement] In ADAPT-PD, the post hoc primary performance threshold was met by 91% receiving dual-threshold and 79% receiving single-threshold adaptive DBS. This measured preservation of good on-time relative to continuous DBS rather than a superiority endpoint. Single-threshold treatment reduced total electrical energy delivered by 15%; this was not a measured 15% battery-longevity extension. (low confidence) — https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaneurology/fullarticle/2839117 · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads
- [statement] A nine-patient double-blind randomized crossover trial using consecutive one-month treatment periods and beta-band dual-threshold control reported no statistically significant adaptive-versus-continuous DBS differences; the authors reported between-patient heterogeneity and called for adequately powered follow-up. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42765432/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads
- [statement] In a randomized double-blind crossover assessment of directional versus omnidirectional stimulation, directional stimulation widened the therapeutic window in 183 of 202 evaluable participants (90.6%), with a mean increase of 41%. Therapeutic window denotes stimulation amplitudes achieving symptom relief without side effects; the study enrolled 234 subjects. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34047410/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads
- [statement] A separate 19-patient randomized directional-versus-omnidirectional crossover trial found no significant differences in primary rigidity or secondary clinical motor outcomes. Its discussion reported 30% lower stimulation intensity with directional stimulation, while chronic motor performance could worsen under the tested directional settings. Wider therapeutic windows should not be equated with universally superior motor outcomes. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-024-00812-0 · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads
- [statement] Both STN and GPi are effective motor-symptom targets; the CNS guideline supports either target for motor treatment rather than a universal target preference. (medium confidence) — https://www.cns.org/guidelines/congress-of-neurological-surgeons-systematic-revie/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK536714/
- [statement] The randomized unilateral COMPARE trial reported no significant STN-versus-GPi difference in its co-primary mood and cognitive outcomes at optimal settings. It also reported adverse mood effects with ventral stimulation in both targets and greater letter-fluency deterioration in nonoptimal STN conditions; these setting-specific findings should not be generalized into inevitable global cognitive decline. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2692580/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming
- [statement] A 2022 Bayesian network meta-analysis associated LCIG and DBS with greater six-month OFF-time and quality-of-life improvement than apomorphine infusion or best medical therapy, with no significant LCIG-versus-DBS difference. Its indirect comparison mixed randomised and non-randomised studies, and carried three-month LCIG/apomorphine trial outcomes forward to six months. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9712309/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS
- [statement] A 2019 meta-analysis of five cohort studies involving 257 patients found no significant LCIG-versus-STN-DBS difference in UPDRS-III motor scores or adverse events; UPDRS-IV improvement favored STN-DBS, with substantial heterogeneity. Lack of significance does not establish equivalence. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6718716/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS
- [statement] In the 12-week active-controlled phase 3 foslevodopa-foscarbidopa trial, the incremental gain in ON time without troublesome dyskinesia versus oral immediate-release levodopa-carbidopa was 1·75 h; the incremental OFF-time reduction was 1·79 h. This was a comparison with oral therapy, not DBS or intestinal infusion. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36402160/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS
- [statement] In that foslevodopa-foscarbidopa trial, adverse events caused premature discontinuation in 16 of 74 infusion participants (22%) versus one of 67 oral-treatment participants (1%); infusion-site events were common. These trial-specific rates should not be used as a cross-device safety league table. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36402160/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS
- [statement] A 2026 systematic review pooling subcutaneous levodopa and foslevodopa regimens found clinically meaningful OFF-time improvement versus oral levodopa, but patient-experience gains were statistically rather than clinically significant, with more infusion-site adverse events; these findings do not compare the pumps directly with DBS. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12853972/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS
- [statement] The 2024 review associates intestinal levodopa therapies with tube displacement, wound problems or infections, abdominal pain and polyneuropathy. It describes apomorphine infusion-site nodules, nausea, somnolence and possible impulse-control disorders; these are therapy-specific risks rather than a single common device-risk profile. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11502575/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS
- [statement] A 2025 retrospective cohort compared 295 people continuing oral therapy with 313 transitioning to device-aided therapy, including 284 DBS and 29 enteral levodopa recipients. Mean 12-month PDQ-39 summary-index change was −5.0 in the device group versus +0.9 in the oral group; these are pooled observational outcomes, not a randomized pump-versus-DBS comparison. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01093-x · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS
- [statement] The 2025 study authors interpret their pooled cohort as showing meaningful quality-of-life improvement after device therapy. Zheng and Liu’s 2026 commentary accepts the observed improvement but questions causal interpretation because of residual candidacy confounding, differing baseline definitions and pooling DBS with enteral levodopa. The commentary identifies possible bias rather than proving the benefits are absent. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01093-x · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS · also: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-026-01342-7
- [statement] In the 27-patient pilot randomized thalamotomy trial, the on-medication treated-hand tremor subscore improved a median 62% after ultrasound versus 22% after sham at 3 months; this is a score reduction, not a percentage of patients cured. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5822192/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy
- [statement] The pallidotomy randomized trial enrolled 94 patients; 65 active-treatment and 22 control patients completed primary assessment. At 3 months, 45 (69%) versus 7 (32%) responded. Response meant at least a 3-point reduction in treated-side off-medication MDS-UPDRS III or on-medication UDysRS, rather than requiring both. (low confidence) — https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2202721 · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36812432/
- [statement] The FDA thalamotomy labeling specifies unilateral ventral intermediate thalamic treatment for medication-refractory tremor in tremor-dominant Parkinson’s disease, in patients at least age 30; it is a tremor indication rather than an indication for all Parkinsonian symptoms. (medium confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S006D.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S037B.pdf
- [statement] Sources differ on unilateral focused ultrasound pallidotomy for Parkinson's disease: the 2022 EAN/MDS-ES guideline's clinical-consensus statement says that unilateral MRgFUS of the pallidum is not recommended, whereas the FDA PMA record for Exablate Neuro lists approval of unilateral pallidotomy for advanced idiopathic Parkinson's disease with a decision date of 10/29/2021, and the NEJM sham-controlled trial reports a response in 45 patients (69%) after ablation versus 7 (32%) after sham. The sources carry different dates, evidence bases and jurisdictions and are recorded side by side, not reconciled. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35791766/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cdrh/cfdocs/cfpma/pma.cfm?id=P150038S014, https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2202721
- [statement] Terkelsen et al. reported improved Lower Body and Gait scores at twelve months, during an open extension rather than a continued sham-controlled comparison; the authors explicitly state that a placebo effect on open-phase patient-reported improvements cannot be excluded. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-68782-w · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Spinal cord stimulation, TMS and tDCS for gait and motor symptoms · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12960713/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Adaptive DBS adjusts stimulation amplitude using neural feedback; the beta-band dual-threshold approach adjusts amplitude according to subthalamic local-field-potential power. (high confidence) — https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-roundup-february-28-2025 · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42765432/
- [statement] The comparative adaptive-DBS literature is heterogeneous: Oehrn and colleagues reported benefit in their four-person personalized gamma-feedback feasibility trial, whereas a nine-person beta-feedback crossover pilot reported no significant treatment differences. These are attributed results from different protocols and populations, not an interchangeable estimate of efficacy. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11826929/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42765432/
- [statement] Two FDA documents give different dates for the aDBS approval: the PMA database lists a decision date of 02/20/2025 for supplement P960009/S478, while the FDA Roundup of February 28, 2025 says that on Friday, February 21 the FDA approved for marketing a software update to Medtronic's Activa, Percept and SenSight DBS system that adds adaptive deep brain stimulation. The one-day difference is recorded as an attributed discrepancy and is not resolved here. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cdrh/cfdocs/cfpma/pma.cfm?id=P960009S478 · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads · also: https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-roundup-february-28-2025
- [statement] The FDA summary of safety and effectiveness for P960009/S478 states that aDBS was not studied in the ADAPT-PD trial with bilaterally implanted neurostimulators, that only subjects with single implanted neurostimulators were eligible, and that the labeling instructs clinicians not to use aDBS with more than one implanted neurostimulator. (low confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf/P960009S478B.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads
- [statement] The 2026 referral consensus states that evidence exists that patients with cognitive impairment may still benefit from DBS for motor symptoms, that there is no data-driven cognitive-performance cut-off for considering DBS, and that mood, anxiety and other psychiatric disturbances do not necessarily exclude candidacy while significant psychiatric symptoms identified by the interdisciplinary team should be addressed prior to surgery. (medium confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-025-01241-3 · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK536714/
- [statement] For conventional ring-contact programming, monopolar review tests contacts individually with the lead contact as cathode and pulse-generator case as anode, identifying benefit and adverse-effect thresholds to select a therapeutic window. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558426/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5632902/
- [statement] Conventional initial monopolar testing commonly holds pulse width at 60 μs and frequency at 130 Hz while amplitude is increased to identify benefit and side-effect thresholds. These are starting settings described in programming literature, not a universal prescription. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558426/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5925823/
- [statement] Two programming reviews describe a programming visit as including questions about symptom changes since the last visit, a clinical examination, and checks of lead type, electrode configuration, impedance and battery; one of them states that there are no validated and well-established programming protocols. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5632902/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5925823/
- [statement] For persistent stimulation-related adverse effects, the programming review recommends checking electrode location, reducing stimulation current and/or changing the active contact; alternative configurations can restrict current spread. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558426/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming
- [statement] Either STN or GPi can be selected for motor benefit; in the randomized trial’s 36-month follow-up, motor improvement was sustained and comparable between targets. (medium confidence) — https://www.cns.org/guidelines/congress-of-neurological-surgeons-systematic-revie/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Deep brain stimulation (STN/GPi): patient selection and programming · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3385495/
- [statement] Delivery route changes invasiveness: subcutaneous apomorphine or levodopa avoids the intestinal tube procedure, intestinal levodopa requires a PEG-J system, and DBS requires intracranial electrode implantation. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11875732/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7592668/
- [statement] Intestinal levodopa bypasses gastric emptying to provide more stable plasma levodopa levels than oral dosing; subcutaneous levodopa is another continuous delivery strategy that avoids surgical jejunal tube placement. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11875732/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12853972/
- [statement] Reviews of device-assisted therapy state that device selection depends on individual patient factors such as age, comorbidities, therapy-specific risks and patient preferences, and a single-centre comparison lists treatment availability, cost of treatment and local expertise as further considerations. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11875732/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10310730/
- [statement] External pumps require daily preparation and site or tube care, often with caregiver support; DBS exchanges this daily external-pump burden for neurosurgery and continuing device follow-up. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7592668/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11875732/
- [statement] A 2023 non-randomised single-centre comparison included 66 patients (13 apomorphine, 19 LCIG, 34 STN-DBS); DBS recipients had better baseline profiles. Quality-of-life and motor outcomes improved with LCIG and DBS, while apomorphine changes were not statistically significant. The baseline imbalance prevents a causal treatment ranking. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10310730/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS
- [statement] OFF-time reduction alone does not guarantee a clinically important quality-of-life gain; this distinction appears in subcutaneous levodopa synthesis and long-term apomorphine experience. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12853972/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS · also: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-021-00194-7
- [statement] Intestinal levodopa gel bypasses swallowing and gastric passage through a jejunal tube and an external pump; DBS requires implantation of electrodes and a pulse generator. Subcutaneous apomorphine and foslevodopa/foscarbidopa avoid the implantation surgery required for these other approaches. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11502575/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6995127/
- [statement] The 2024 individualized-treatment review describes foslevodopa/foscarbidopa as a soluble prodrug formulation permitting continuous subcutaneous delivery over a 24-hour period. It reports infusion-site erythema, nodules, cellulitis and pain, as well as visual hallucinations, among adverse effects. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11502575/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS
- [statement] Daily device work matters in treatment choice: LCIG and apomorphine pumps require cartridge changes and handling, often with relative or nursing support. DBS still requires specialist follow-up and rechargeable systems require charging; discussions should include maintenance, lifestyle and caregiver needs. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11502575/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3825542/
- [statement] The Michael J. Fox Foundation reported on February 3, 2026 that ND0612, an under-the-skin infusion of levodopa and carbidopa, had received a second FDA Complete Response Letter; it states that the FDA sent a first Complete Response Letter in June 2024 and, after the company's May 2025 resubmission, issued the second in October 2025. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-02-03) — https://www.michaeljfox.org/news/second-fda-response-letter-issued-nd0612-therapy · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS
- [statement] Thalamotomy trial safety findings included two cases of mild hemiparesis from internal-capsule heating that improved, alongside persistent orofacial paresthesia, finger paresthesia and ataxia. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5822192/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy
- [statement] Pallidotomy durability was assessed in an open-label extension: 30 of 39 assessed initial responders still responded at 12 months. This denominator excludes initial nonresponders and unassessed responders. (low confidence) — https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2202721 · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy
- [statement] Pallidotomy-related adverse events included dysarthria, gait disturbance, loss of taste, visual disturbance and facial weakness; investigators called for longer and larger trials. (medium confidence) — https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2202721 · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36812432/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11422448/
- [statement] The July 3, 2025 FDA S037 expansion concerns pallidothalamic tractotomy, including a contralateral procedure staged at least 6 months later in eligible patients aged at least 30. It must not be described as blanket approval of bilateral GPi pallidotomy or bilateral Parkinson thalamotomy. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-07-03) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S037B.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cdrh/cfdocs/cfpma/pma.cfm?id=P150038S014
- [statement] NICE HTG733, published December 18, 2024, restricts focused ultrasound thalamotomy for moderate-to-severe Parkinson’s tremor to formal research approved by a research ethics committee. That NHS recommendation is jurisdiction-specific and should be distinguished from FDA device approval. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2024-12-18) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/htg733/chapter/1-Recommendations · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S037B.pdf
- [statement] MR-guided focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy are lesioning procedures: focused acoustic energy heats and ablates a selected brain target, with MRI thermometry and clinical testing guiding delivery. Incisionless delivery still entails destruction of brain tissue. (medium confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S006D.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://www.e-jmd.org/journal/view.php?number=583
- [statement] Durability and generalizability remain uncertain: the pallidotomy trial called for longer and larger studies, and the systematic review recommends follow-up beyond one year with larger samples and controlled, blinded designs. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36812432/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11422448/
- [statement] Patient selection requires more than symptom severity: the tremor-dominant Parkinson’s prescriber information requires MRI suitability, ability to tolerate and communicate during treatment, and screening for bleeding risks, prolonged immobilization and skull-density constraints. (medium confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S006D.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S037B.pdf
- [statement] Exact skull-density eligibility must be taken from the relevant labeling: the June 2018 tremor-dominant Parkinson’s prescriber document lists 0.45 (±0.05) or less, whereas the July 2025 S037 document lists less than 0.40. These target- and revision-specific documents should not be collapsed into one universal cutoff. (medium confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S006D.pdf · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Focused ultrasound thalamotomy and pallidotomy · also: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf15/P150038S037B.pdf
- [statement] A randomized double-blind SCS evaluation (abstract copyright 2025) was stopped for futility after eight implantations and seven completed blinded evaluations; active stimulation did not significantly improve Timed Up and Go or the other measured outcomes. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40172032/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Spinal cord stimulation, TMS and tDCS for gait and motor symptoms
- [statement] In the MicroBurst feasibility trial, twelve participants were randomized to six months of active stimulation or sham. The primary clinical PIGD endpoint was not met, although feasibility and safety endpoints were met. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12960713/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Spinal cord stimulation, TMS and tDCS for gait and motor symptoms · also: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-68782-w
- [statement] The blinded comparisons in the Carra 2025 and Terkelsen 2026 trials did not establish a significant gait benefit from their tested SCS protocols; these findings are protocol-specific and do not prove that every possible SCS approach is ineffective. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40172032/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Spinal cord stimulation, TMS and tDCS for gait and motor symptoms · also: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-68782-w, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12960713/
- [statement] SCS implantation carries procedural risks: Terkelsen et al. reported four serious adverse events related to implantation, comprising dural puncture, two lead misplacements, and perioperative pain; dural puncture and lead misplacement required repeat surgery. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-68782-w · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Spinal cord stimulation, TMS and tDCS for gait and motor symptoms · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12960713/
- [statement] A randomized double-blind sham-controlled trial (abstract copyright 2019) allocated thirty patients with freezing of gait to ten sessions of real or sham 10 Hz rTMS over the supplementary motor area; ON-medication assessments showed improvements in freezing questionnaire, motor, and gait outcomes during follow-up through four weeks. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31689588/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Spinal cord stimulation, TMS and tDCS for gait and motor symptoms
- [statement] An rTMS meta-analysis of randomized trials searching through December 2024 included nineteen studies and 547 participants. It found benefits for freezing, gait speed and UPDRS-III, but not UPDRS total or TUG; publication-bias testing was positive for gait speed. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41517414/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Spinal cord stimulation, TMS and tDCS for gait and motor symptoms
- [statement] Liu et al. (2021) synthesized twenty-one tDCS studies involving 736 participants and concluded that evidence for motor improvement was insufficient; pooled UPDRS-III, Timed Up and Go, balance, and gait outcomes did not establish a motor benefit. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8584149/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Spinal cord stimulation, TMS and tDCS for gait and motor symptoms
- [statement] The tDCS review reports headache, tingling, forehead burning, and a small number of first-degree burns in included studies; the authors reported no serious consequences from these events, so noninvasive stimulation should not be described as having no adverse effects. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8584149/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Spinal cord stimulation, TMS and tDCS for gait and motor symptoms
- [statement] Implanted SCS delivers electrical stimulation through an epidural lead connected to a subcutaneous pulse generator; its use for Parkinsonian gait is distinct from its established pain indication. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12960713/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Spinal cord stimulation, TMS and tDCS for gait and motor symptoms
- [statement] rTMS has shown benefits for selected gait and motor outcomes in a randomized treadmill-training trial and a pooled analysis; benefit should be interpreted by outcome and stimulation protocol. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8470277/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Spinal cord stimulation, TMS and tDCS for gait and motor symptoms · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41517414/
- [statement] In a randomized trial of fifty-one participants, twelve sessions of 1Hz or 25Hz rTMS before treadmill training improved fastest walking speed more than sham at one day and three months; this evaluates rTMS as a rehabilitation adjunct. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8470277/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Spinal cord stimulation, TMS and tDCS for gait and motor symptoms
- [statement] Evidence reviewed here does not establish reliable tDCS benefit for Parkinsonian motor function: a randomized freezing-of-gait trial missed its primary endpoint and a 2021 systematic review found insufficient motor-function evidence. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34406695/ · keywords: Parkinson's disease surgical and device therapies: deep brain stimulation, adaptive DBS, focused ultrasound, levodopa pumps and infusions, and neuromodulation for gait, Spinal cord stimulation, TMS and tDCS for gait and motor symptoms · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8584149/
